page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 256.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. The server includes a bundled local SSD storage capacity of 2458 GB, managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance and memory bandwidth capabilities. The instance achieves a strong rating in multi-core CPU execution, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 62,149.0 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,422.0. Large-block memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, reaching 291.88 GB/sec for read-only and 134.9 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,649.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,899.49. This indicates a performance profile optimized for parallelized workloads rather than single-threaded execution speed.

The combination of 64 dedicated vCPUs, 256.0 GB of RAM, and 2458 GB of local SSD storage makes this server appropriate for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and static web serving. Passmark database operations scored in the top tier at 30,145.69, and Redis SET operations reached 62.01 million operations per second. While the server delivers strong multi-threaded decompression and ray tracing capabilities, its LLM inference speeds for larger models remain average, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled high-capacity local SSD and high resource density provide a consolidated platform for data-intensive applications without requiring external storage attachments.
